items.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark for interpreting raw wet-lab evidence. Scores and model comparisons are company-reported; the article also documents remaining errors and limitations.

items.title: The components of agent memory
items.summary: Anthropic described a memory hierarchy for agents and reported experiments in which offline “dreaming” corrected notes and built searchable representations. Results and implementation lessons are company-reported.

items.title: How NVIDIA Open Source Tools Are Helping Researchers Build Next-Generation 6G Networks
items.summary: NVIDIA described open-source 5G/6G tools used to research wireless systems for robotics, signal reception and capacity planning. Adoption, download and performance figures are company- and partner-reported.

items.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.summary: OpenAI announced a partnership with Hacktron to test high-priority areas of its systems, especially third-party service integrations, using expanded Daybreak Red access. Scope and expected benefits are company-reported.

items.title: Teaching AI to build scientific models
items.summary: Anthropic published a guest article on using AI to build, constrain and interpret scientific models, emphasizing that fitting data is not sufficient for scientific understanding. Examples reflect the authors’ analysis.

items.title: Design the Muse App, Just for You
items.summary: Meta introduced Spaces in Muse, custom experiences users create from a description and arrange in the app. Connected spaces can update in the background. Availability and capabilities are company-reported.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT‑6 Cyber for authorized security research, reporting gains in vulnerability discovery and scope adherence. Benchmark and real-world results are company-reported, not independently validated.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.summary: Google launched Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with native video clips up to 15 seconds, conversational editing and general availability via the Gemini API and Cloud. Pricing and performance claims are Google’s.

items.title: AI for scientific discovery: How researchers use Claude
items.summary: Anthropic analyzed 207,000 Claude and Claude Code research sessions with privacy-preserving methods, describing how scientists use AI across fields and tasks. Findings and scenarios are company-reported.

items.title: Le Chonk brings the brains. Studio puts it to work.
items.summary: Mistral expanded Studio with managed agents and apps, workflows, enterprise context, observability and evaluations, deployable in cloud, VPC or on premises. Adoption and time-savings claims are company- and customer-reported.

items.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
items.summary: NVIDIA described developers using frontier AI agents with Omniverse libraries to build and test editable 3D assets, robotic disassembly and simulation workflows. Examples and outcomes are company-reported.

items.title: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents
items.summary: NVIDIA presented Vera CPU performance for agentic workloads and early partner tests. Speed, throughput and efficiency figures are NVIDIA- and partner-reported, not independently validated.

items.title: Give Your Muse a Voice
items.summary: Meta is rolling out real-time voice and expressive avatars for Muse in the U.S. across mobile, web and Mac, with voice-only and avatar modes. Availability and capabilities are company-reported.

items.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
items.summary: NVIDIA described a full-stack memory hierarchy for agentic inference, spanning HBM, CPU memory, storage and Dynamo. Efficiency and throughput comparisons are company-reported.

items.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
items.summary: OpenAI described partnerships with four Australian universities expanding access to ChatGPT Edu and Codex, AI curricula and governed classroom use. Survey figures and program outcomes are OpenAI-commissioned or institution-reported.

items.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
items.summary: OpenAI says an autonomous security pipeline found and validated 948 Linux privilege-escalation vulnerabilities and produced patches. The results and costs are company-reported, not independently validated.

items.title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
items.summary: OpenAI made GPT-5.6 Cyber available to approved Daybreak Red customers in AWS GovCloud (US-East) for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation and security testing, with practitioner review required.

items.title: Introducing Images 2.6
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Images 2.6 in ChatGPT, Codex and the API, with reported gains in instruction following, editing and visual reasoning. Quality and performance claims are company-reported.

items.title: Investigating vault particles with Claude
items.summary: Anthropic reports using Claude to help determine the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle. The work is described in a submitted preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
items.summary: OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Pierre, whose open-source Trees and Diffs libraries are used in Codex. The company plans to bring Pierre’s code review and storage capabilities into Codex after closing.

items.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world

items.title: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Cheminformatics Skills for Antigravity to automate literature search, molecular analysis and candidate design. Timings and results are company-reported; proposals still need experimental validation.

items.title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It

items.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
items.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open research prototype using cryptographic proofs to verify that responses came from a committed model. Performance results are the team’s.

items.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
